entry.pre_arrival: Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC) online within 3 days before arrival, free (or by QR code on arrival).
entry.next_check: Read the exemption length from Taiwan's Bureau of Consular Affairs.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the New Taiwan Dollar (NTD). Declare amounts over USD10,000 or equivalent. ATMs are widely available in cities and provincial centres. International credit cards are usually accepted in hotels, restaurants and higher-end shops, especially in cities and larger towns.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and include the death penalty, life imprisonment and heavy fines. Don't use or carry any illegal drugs, including illegal prescription medication. Carrying certain prescription drugs can result in heavy fines and long jail sentences (see 'Health').
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: If you're involved in a legal dispute, you won't be allowed to leave Taiwan until the dispute is settled. This includes minor offences. You may be detained on arrival if you have an outstanding arrest warrant in Taiwan. Legal processes can be long. Local authorities won't accept bonds or deposits to guarantee court appearances.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Some prescription medications are illegal in Taiwan. Authorities may jail or fine you for carrying these medications. If you plan to take medication, check if it's legal in Taiwan. Taiwan Customs gives advice on limits and documents you'll need.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: If you plan to drive in Taiwan, you must get an International Driving Permit (IDP) before you arrive. You can drive for up to 30 days with an IDP and a current Australian licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted). If you plan to stay longer, apply for an extension at the nearest motor vehicle office in Taiwan. Check Taiwan’s Highway Bureau for information on how to apply for a Taiwanese Driver's Licence.
laws.heading: Driving permit

meetings.detail: Business and sales meetings and client visits are permitted, as long as nothing is paid in Taiwan.

conference.detail: Attending conferences and workshops is permitted.

unpaid-speaking.route: Work permit, applied for by the host
unpaid-speaking.detail: The Ministry of Labor treats speakers as workers who need a work permit, paid or not; visa-exempt entry doesn't change that.
unpaid-speaking.next: Ask the host to apply to the Workforce Development Agency.

paid-speaking.route: Work permit, applied for by the host
paid-speaking.detail: The Ministry of Labor treats speakers as workers who need a work permit, paid or not; visa-exempt entry doesn't change that.

book-launch.route: Work permit for any talk or appearance
book-launch.detail: The Ministry of Labor treats speakers as workers who need a work permit, paid or not; visa-exempt entry doesn't change that.
book-launch.next: Ask the publisher to apply, or keep to private meetings.

ai-teaching.route: Work permit, unless lecturing at a university with Ministry of Education approval
ai-teaching.detail: Teaching is work. Article 48 exempts lecturing or academic research at a public or registered private university approved by the Ministry of Education.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the host whether its approval covers you, or to apply for a permit.

remote-work.next: Ask the place's immigration authority (no office in Australia is listed) which visa covers it, in writing.

trade.detail: Visiting clients and sales meetings are permitted.

artist.route: Visa-exempt entry for invited non-profit performances (30 days or less)
artist.detail: Non-profit artistic or cultural performances or sporting events at the invitation of a central competent authority, for 30 days or less, count as permitted; paid commercial work needs a work permit.
artist.next: Ask the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office.

mixed-mission.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
mixed-mission.next: Ask the place's immigration authority (no office in Australia is listed) which visa covers it, in writing.

filming.route: Visas for the crew plus the city's filming application
filming.detail: Foreign crews follow each city's filming application (for example New Taipei City) and need visas under Taiwan's immigration rules; the national Film in Taiwan program helps with permits.
filming.next: Contact the city film office for the location.

research.route: Ask the place's immigration authority (no office in Australia is listed)
research.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
research.next: Ask the place's immigration authority (no office in Australia is listed) which visa covers it, in writing.

volunteering.detail: The Ministry of Labor treats volunteers, speakers and performers as workers who need work permits, paid or not.
volunteering.next: Ask the host to apply for a permit.
